sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 (2010)
cleanIntro: This is the FLINT LOCK Hawken. It is the same hooked-breech sidelock as the cap lock rifle — barrel off by one wedge pin, breech plug stays in the barrel — but the ignition end is a different machine: a frizzen, a pan, a touchhole and a touchhole bushing instead of a nipple and cap. Thompson/Center gives the flintlock its own priming and firing sections and its own rule about oil, and that rule is the opposite of what you would do everywhere else on the rifle.

steps.title: Drop the ramrod down the bore to check for a charge
steps.action: The sidelock owner's chamber check. An empty barrel lets the ramrod stand about an inch proud of the muzzle; a charged barrel stops it short of that.
steps.caution: Mark the ramrod at the muzzle line for an empty barrel so this becomes a glance you can trust.
steps.quote: VERIFY THAT THE RIFLE BARREL IS NOT LOADED BY DROPPING THE RAMROD DOWN THE BORE. THE RAMROD WILL PROTRUDE ABOUT ONE INCH FROM AN UNCHARGED BARREL.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41

steps.title: Open the frizzen and clear the pan
steps.action: On the flintlock, unpriming means opening the frizzen and getting the priming powder out of the pan and the touchhole. There is no cap to pull — the priming charge is loose powder and it must physically leave the gun.
steps.quote: Ensure that the gun is unprimed. Remove the cap from the nipple on the cap lock or open the frizzen and remove any priming powder that may be present from the flint lock.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Unloading a Charge from the Thompson/Center Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — p.34
steps.warn: Never dry-fire a flint lock when the barrel is charged. A spark from dry-firing could cause an accidental discharge.

steps.title: Clear the touchhole with the pick
steps.action: Powder residue crusts inside the ignition channel and partially blocks it. Work the touchhole pick in and out until the full diameter is open — the manual asks for this before loading and after every shot, and it is also how you confirm the channel is clear before cleaning.
steps.quote: Use your touchhole pick before loading initially and after each subsequent shot.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Priming the Hawken™ Flint Lock — p.30

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Pull the ramrod from the thimbles under the barrel and set it aside before the barrel leaves the stock.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod - set it aside.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Pull the wedge pin
steps.action: A single wedge pin through the forend holds the barrel down. Tap it partially out from the far side until you can grip it, then draw it clear. There is only one and the rifle does not go back together without it.
steps.caution: Tap gently with a punch smaller than the escutcheon, or you will bruise the wood around it.
steps.quote: Pull out the wedge pin. It may be necessary to tap it partially out from the other side in order to grasp the pin and pull it the rest of the way out.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Lift the barrel and pull it forward off the hooked breech
steps.action: Lift at the muzzle, then draw the barrel forward. That forward motion unhooks the breech plug from its slot in the tang. The plug stays in the barrel throughout — it is never unscrewed for cleaning on this rifle.
steps.aside: This is the full extent of the disassembly the manual publishes. The lock stays in the stock.
steps.quote: Lift the barrel up as shown (Figure 35) and pull it forward away from the lock assembly. Pull the barrel forward, thus pulling the breech plug out of the breech plug slot in the tang.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Run the bore with the supplied jag
steps.action: Jag on the ramrod, patch soaked in black-powder solvent, worked the length of the bore until the patches come out clean, then dry patches until it is dry.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive rather than merely dirty, and fouling builds shot to shot until a ball will not seat.
steps.quote: Use the cleaning jag that was provided with the Hawken™, and a cleaning patch saturated with a bore cleaner like Thompson/Center’s Number 13® Bore Cleaner (Figure 33).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Field Cleaning — p.37

steps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
steps.action: With the barrel off the stock, stand its muzzle in a pan of hot soapy water and pump a wet patch from the breech end. The barrel acts as its own pump — this is what the hooked breech is for.
steps.caution: Dry the bore completely before oiling. Water left in a black-powder barrel rusts fast.
steps.quote: Next in the cleaning process; fill a pan with hot soapy water.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Take out the touchhole bushing, not a nipple
steps.action: The flintlock's equivalent of the nipple is the touchhole bushing. It comes out for cleaning along with the matching threads in the barrel, then dries thoroughly and goes back in.
steps.aside: One instruction, two locks. Yours is the touchhole bushing — the nipple belongs to the cap lock rifle.
steps.quote: Remove the nipple on the cap lock model (or the touchhole bushing on the flint lock) and clean it and the corresponding threads in the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.40

steps.title: Leave the frizzen, pan and flint bone dry — no oil, ever
steps.action: This is the flintlock's own rule and it reverses everything else you do while cleaning. Oil anywhere in the ignition area kills the spark. If lubricant reaches these parts during cleaning, degrease them rather than wiping them.
steps.quote: Make sure the surfaces of the frizzen, the pan, and the flint are free of any oil or lubricant, and as dry as possible. Never wipe down these parts with any type of lubricant.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Priming the Hawken™ Flint Lock — p.29
steps.warn: A dry ignition area is the key to good ignition with a flint lock. Use a good degreaser if oil reaches the frizzen, pan or flint.

steps.title: Wipe the lock and trigger area down and dry it
steps.action: Flash from the pan throws residue over the lock every shot. Wipe the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver area, dry it, and keep any oil off the ignition surfaces.
steps.caution: Keep lubricant light and away from the pan. Heavy oil congeals in cold weather and slows the hammer fall.
steps.quote: Thoroughly wipe any powder residue from the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver. Dry the parts thoroughly.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.40

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off the stock, bore flushed and dry, touchhole bushing out and clean, ignition surfaces degreased. That is everything Thompson/Center publishes for this rifle. Reassembly, including the one step that reliably goes wrong, is in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM beyond the procedures outlined in this manual.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

deepSteps.title: Check the flint before the rifle goes away
deepSteps.action: A dull flint is the flintlock's equivalent of a dead battery, and cleaning is when you notice it. Keep the leading edge sharp by knapping, and make sure it sits square in the jaws.
deepSteps.quote: Sharp flints are a must for quick, positive ignition. Keep the front of the flint sharp by knapping if necessary.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Priming the Hawken™ Flint Lock — p.29

deepSteps.title: Clear the ignition channel to full diameter
deepSteps.action: After firing, a crust of powder residue builds in the ignition channel and partially blocks it. That crust must come out and the channel be opened to its full diameter, or ignition gets unreliable in a way no amount of fresh priming powder fixes.
deepSteps.aside: The manual's own words on the crust: it must be removed, and the channel cleared out to the full diameter, before re-loading, in order to get reliable ignition.
deepSteps.quote: Open the frizzen and proceed as follows.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Priming the Hawken™ Flint Lock — p.30

deepSteps.title: Seat the hooked breech before the barrel goes down
deepSteps.action: The step that goes wrong. The breech plug hook must be fully into the hole in the tang BEFORE the barrel tips down into the channel. Resistance when bringing forend and barrel together is the hook not seated — re-seat it, never force it.
deepSteps.quote: Grasp the barrel, and insert the hooked breech into the hole in the tang, making sure that the breech plug fits closely against the tang before tipping the barrel down into the forearm channel.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41
deepSteps.warn: Heavy resistance means the hooked breech plug is not fully seated in the tang. Stop and check.

deepSteps.title: Refit the wedge pin
deepSteps.action: Hold barrel and forend together and push the wedge pin through the escutcheon. It fits snugly and may need a gentle tap to fully engage.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the barrel and forearm of the stock together with your hand, and insert the wedge pin through the escutcheon hole in the forend.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag until they come out clean
Muzzle in hot soapy water, pump a wet patch from the breech end to flush the barrel
Dry patches until the bore is completely dry
Light lubricant on the bore once dry

cleaning.name: Ignition — keep this dry
tasks: Remove the touchhole bushing and clean it and the threads in the barrel
Clear the ignition channel to its full diameter with the touchhole pick
Degrease the frizzen, the pan and the flint — no oil or lubricant on any of them
Knap the flint sharp and check it sits square in the jaws
Dry every ignition part thoroughly before reassembly

cleaning.name: Lock and exterior
tasks: Wipe powder residue from the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver, then dry
Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the trigger guard assembly, then dry and lightly oil
Remove exterior fouling with a cloth dampened with bore cleaner, dry, then a light oil — keeping oil away from the pan and frizzen

reassembly: Refit the touchhole bushing into the barrel
Insert the hooked breech into the hole in the tang and confirm the plug sits closely against the tang
Tip the barrel down into the barrel channel in the stock
Hold barrel and forend together and push the wedge pin through the escutcheon, tapping gently to fully engage
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
Degrease the frizzen, pan and flint one last time before the rifle is primed
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, re-assemble and check the hammer and trigger mechanism for proper function before loading and firing. Confirm the frizzen closes and springs open cleanly, and that the ramrod still protrudes about one inch from the muzzle.
